key_insight: In this systematic review screening comparison, Loon Lens outperformed Catchii at title/abstract screening, and higher AI confidence scores were linked to better agreement with human reviewers.
clinical_relevance: AI screening tools may help speed systematic reviews, but performance varies enough that teams should test the tool they plan to use before relying on it for evidence synthesis.
method: De novo review question on air pollutants and Parkinson’s disease.
Compared two agentic AI tools (Loon LensTM and Catchii) against human screening at title/abstract level.
Compared Loon Lens with humans at full-text screening and analyzed confidence vs disagreement.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, concordance, kappa, and F1, with human screening as the reference standard and confidence scores modeled against agreement.
watch_item: Results may not generalize across topics or tools, and AI screening decisions still showed meaningful disagreement with humans, especially at full-text stage.
paper_title: Comparing Artificial Intelligence versus Human Screening in Systematic Reviews
